stories.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
stories.summary: SpaceX’s Starship returned to its Florida launch site after a 22-hour orbital flight and was caught in midair by the pad’s giant mechanical arms. The first-of-its-kind capture, performed by arms nicknamed “chopsticks,” demonstrated a key part of SpaceX’s plan to make Starship rapidly reusable. Al Jazeera, the BBC, the Washington Examiner and the Washington Times all reported the milestone.

stories.title: Cocaine-Funded Gangs Shake Colombia Years After Peace Pact
stories.summary: Cocaine-funded armed groups are carrying out attacks against civilians in Colombia eight years after a peace agreement removed a major rebel organisation from the conflict. The Wall Street Journal attributes the militias’ strength in part to state inaction after the accord. The violence shows how other armed groups have filled space left by the former rebel force.

links.headline: Cocaine-Funded Gangs Shake Colombia Years After Peace Pact
links.excerpt: Attacks by powerful militias against civilians reflect the state’s inaction eight years after a peace accord removed a powerful rebel group from the field.

stories.title: Canada Is Becoming a Fentanyl Exporter, and a Target for Trump
stories.summary: Fentanyl is increasingly being manufactured in and trafficked from Canada, drawing scrutiny from President Donald Trump. The Wall Street Journal reports that Canada is becoming an exporter of the drug. However, the quantities remain small compared with fentanyl flows linked to Mexico.

links.headline: Canada Is Becoming a Fentanyl Exporter, and a Target for Trump
links.excerpt: The drug is increasingly manufactured in and trafficked from the U.S.’s northern neighbor, though the numbers remain small compared with Mexico.
